formats.key: mintWithAttestation((uint256 chainId, uint256 attestationId, bytes32 userId, address asset, uint256 price, uint256 quantity, uint256 expiration, uint8 side, bytes32 additionalData) quote, bytes signature, address depositToken, uint256 depositTokenAmount)
effects: If depositToken is not USDon, the contract takes exactly depositTokenAmount of depositToken from the signer and sends it to the USDonManager to buy USDon.
If depositToken is USDon, the contract takes quote.quantity * quote.price / 1e18 USDon from the signer and ignores depositTokenAmount.
The signer receives exactly quote.quantity of the GM token quote.asset, minted to msg.sender.
On the non-USDon path, the signer receives a refund in USDon (not in the deposit token) of any USDon bought above quote.quantity * quote.price.
The transferFrom spends the signer's existing allowance of the deposit token to the GMTokenManager.
The attestation id is marked as used; the call reverts after quote.expiration.
formats.shown: Mint {quantity} {GM token} using {depositTokenAmount} {depositToken}, with the GM token, both amounts and the quote expiry as fields; price, refund and recipient are not shown.

findings.title: mintWithAttestation shows depositTokenAmount, but with USDon as deposit token it takes quantity times price instead.
findings.evidence: GMTokenManager.sol mintWithAttestation: `if (depositToken == address(usdon)) { IERC20(usdon).safeTransferFrom(_msgSender(), address(this), mintUSDonValue);` with `mintUSDonValue = (quote.quantity * quote.price) / GM_NORMALIZER`. Descriptor: field `depositTokenAmount` 'Deposit Amount' (tokenAmount, tokenPath depositToken) and interpolatedIntent 'Mint {quote.quantity} using {depositTokenAmount}'; `quote.price` is `visible: never`.
findings.fix: Show `quote.price` (for example format `unit`, base USD, decimals 18, label 'Price per GM Token'), and relabel the deposit field 'Deposit Amount (USDon: quantity x price)'. Add a test case with depositToken = USDon.

findings.title: mintWithAttestation hides the USDon refund of excess deposit that the signer receives.
findings.evidence: GMTokenManager.sol mintWithAttestation: `uint256 refund = receivedOnUsd - mintUSDonValue; if (refund > 0) { IERC20(usdon).safeTransfer(_msgSender(), refund); }`. Case 0: signer receives 0.037783085287415162 USDon; case 2: signer receives 1 wei USDon. Nothing on screen mentions USDon.
findings.fix: Make `quote.price` visible so the signer can see the cost basis, and state the refund in the intent, e.g. intent 'Mint GM Token, excess refunded in USDon'.

findings.title: mintWithAttestation hides quote.price, the signed price that sets the USDon cost and the refund.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: `{"path": "quote.price", "label": "Quote Price", "visible": "never"}`. Code: `mintUSDonValue = (quote.quantity * quote.price) / GM_NORMALIZER` decides the refund and, on the USDon path, the amount taken.
findings.fix: Set `quote.price` visible with format `unit` (base 'USD', decimals 18) and label 'Price per GM Token'.

findings.title: mintWithAttestation tests only non-USDon deposits; the USDon branch that ignores depositTokenAmount is not tested.
findings.evidence: Cases 0 and 2 use USDC (0xa0b8…eb48) and BSC USDT (0x55d3…7955). The `depositToken == address(usdon)` branch changes the amount taken.
findings.fix: Add a test case with depositToken = USDon (0xAcE8E719899F6E91831B18AE746C9A965c2119F1 on Ethereum).

cases.notes: USDC out 3778.299782 and MSFTon in 9.258010320826351 shown right. USDon refund 0.0378 not shown.
USDT out and GOOGLon in shown right. Existing USDT allowance spent (Approval event) not shown; reader guessed a prior approval. 1 wei USDon refund not shown.

formats.key: redeemWithAttestation((uint256 chainId, uint256 attestationId, bytes32 userId, address asset, uint256 price, uint256 quantity, uint256 expiration, uint8 side, bytes32 additionalData) quote, bytes signature, address receiveToken, uint256 minimumReceiveAmount)
effects: The contract takes exactly quote.quantity of the GM token quote.asset from the signer and burns it.
If receiveToken is not USDon, the signer receives the receiveToken amount returned by USDonManager.redeem, which gets minimumReceiveAmount as its minimum.
If receiveToken is USDon, the signer receives quote.quantity * quote.price / 1e18 USDon and minimumReceiveAmount is not checked.
The transferFrom spends the signer's existing allowance of the GM token to the GMTokenManager.
The attestation id is marked as used; the call reverts after quote.expiration.
formats.shown: Redeem {quantity} {GM token} for {minimumReceiveAmount} {receiveToken}+, with the GM token, amounts and quote expiry as fields; price and recipient are hidden.

findings.title: redeemWithAttestation shows a minimum received that the code does not check when receiveToken is USDon.
findings.evidence: GMTokenManager.sol redeemWithAttestation: `if (receiveToken == address(usdon)) { IERC20(usdon).safeTransfer(_msgSender(), redemptionUSDonValue); }` and minimumReceiveAmount is only passed to `usdonManager.redeem` in the else branch. NatSpec: 'ONLY applicable if the user requests a non-USDon token'. Descriptor shows 'Min Receive Amount' and 'Redeem {quote.quantity} for {minimumReceiveAmount}+'; `quote.price` is `visible: never`.
findings.fix: Show `quote.price` (format `unit`, base USD, decimals 18, label 'Price per GM Token') so the USDon amount is checkable, and relabel the minimum 'Min Receive (not applied for USDon)'. Add a test case with receiveToken = USDon.

findings.title: redeemWithAttestation interpolated intent uses a trailing '+' that readers do not understand as 'at least'.
findings.evidence: interpolatedIntent 'Redeem {quote.quantity} for {minimumReceiveAmount}+' renders 'for 2307.598294 USDC+' (case 1) and '81.751666303999999999 USDT+' (case 3). Both blind readers listed the meaning of '+' as unsure.
findings.fix: Change interpolatedIntent to 'Redeem {quote.quantity} for at least {minimumReceiveAmount}'.

findings.title: redeemWithAttestation hides quote.price, which sets the USDon value redeemed.
findings.evidence: Descriptor: `quote.price` `visible: never`. Code: `redemptionUSDonValue = (quote.quantity * quote.price) / GM_NORMALIZER` is the amount sent to the signer on the USDon path and redeemed via USDonManager otherwise.
findings.fix: Set `quote.price` visible with format `unit` (base 'USD', decimals 18) and label 'Price per GM Token'.

findings.title: redeemWithAttestation tests only non-USDon receive tokens; the USDon branch that skips the minimum is untested.
findings.evidence: Cases 1 and 3 use USDC and BSC USDT as receiveToken. The `receiveToken == address(usdon)` branch ignores minimumReceiveAmount.
findings.fix: Add a test case with receiveToken = USDon.

cases.notes: COINon out 11.074373021490512 shown right; USDC in 2307.621370 is above the shown minimum 2307.598294. Spend of the existing COINon allowance (Approval event, 26877 left) not shown; it is the prerequisite of the transfer.
SLVon out 1.0208 and USDT in 81.751666304 (at least the shown minimum) shown right.

couldNotCheck: USDonManager (address in storage `usdonManager`) is not in the directory: its `subscribe` decides the USDon bought and so the refund to the signer in mintWithAttestation, and its `redeem` enforces minimumReceiveAmount and the amount returned to the signer in redeemWithAttestation.
